description: Non-stationary by REGIME, not by preemption frequency: Phase A = urgent high-priority jobs that happen to be LONG (PRIORITY must run them first; SJF/FCFS get it wrong); Phase B = equal-priority batch with varied bursts (SJF minimises waiting; PRIORITY degenerates to FCFS and blocks behind a long job). The per-phase best algorithms (PRIORITY vs SJF) neither preempt excessively, so any adaptation headroom should SURVIVE a context-switch cost — unlike the RR-vs-FCFS kind. Default start = PRIORITY (right for Phase A), switch once to SJF for Phase B.
